title: Microbundle Release Cadence and Interlock Calendar (Feb 2026) — Draft
content:
Purpose:
This doc defines a compact, repeatable process for bundling small changes (microfeatures, config flips, infra knobs) into a single microbundle release window. Goal: reduce cognitive overhead of many tiny deploys while retaining low blast radius and fast rollback + clear interlock across teams.

Scope and when to use microbundles:
- Target: changes that are low-to-medium risk (non-breaking API changes, front-end flags, infra upgrade shards, model variant defaults, observability flags).
- Avoid: DB migrations that touch schema, large model swaps, quota or pricing changes, cross-region infra changes.
- Typical bundle size: 3–8 items. Aim for <15 total token-impacting endpoints.

Cadence and calendar model (example Feb 2026 run):
- Weekly microbundle window: Thursdays 10:00–16:00 PT (two 3-hour execution slots with 1h buffer).
- Planning cutover: Tuesday 17:00 PT — final bundle contents locked; last-minute exceptions need approval from release steward.
- Dry-run: Wednesday 09:30–10:30 PT — smoke scripts executed against staging mirrored traffic.
- Canary ramp: Slot A: 10:00–12:00 PT (5% traffic), Slot B: 13:00–15:00 PT (25% traffic). Slow ramp and hold for key SLO checks.
- Post-release observation: 16:00–18:00 PT — consolidated notes, rollback decision window, and evening wrap.

Sample four-week calendar (dates show the Thursday release window):
- 2026-02-05: Microbundle 2026-02-05 — items: RE-4789, RE-4792, RE-4801 (small console UX tweak, batcher tuning, canary retry backoff).
- 2026-02-12: Microbundle 2026-02-12 — items: RE-4810, RE-4814 (dedicated autoscaler param change, telemetry tag additions).
- 2026-02-19: Microbundle 2026-02-19 — items: RE-4821, RE-4826, RE-4829 (promote model-quant profile, rollout config, api surface doc update).
- 2026-02-26: Microbundle 2026-02-26 — catch-up window / emergency lane (reserve for deferred items).

Interlock checklist (coordination across teams) — to be completed before Tuesday 17:00 PT lock:
- Owners for each item assigned (owner + backup).
- JIRA status: all microbundle tickets in state "ready-for-release" and linked to the Microbundle epic.
- PRs: merge queue cleared and release notes snippet provided in PR description.
- Telemetry: dashboards created/updated (latency, error-rate, 95p/99p, model quality sample alerts).
- Rollback plan: per-item rollback commands and expected impact documented in ticket.
- Communication: Slack #release-orchestra pinned timeline + customer success heads notified for visible customers.

Preflight checklist (Wednesday dry-run and morning of release):
- Run smoke suite against staging mirror (smoke ID: MB-2026-02).
- Validate token-level cost telemetry sampling is active for changed endpoints.
- Run 5 runbooks: cold-start latency, kv-cache hit ratio, batching tail latency, model-fallback route test, auth token rotation test.
- Confirm SLI baseline snapshots captured 24h before release window.
- Verify alert throttles set to avoid noisy alerts during canary ramp.

Canary ramp gates (stop criteria at each hold):
- Gate A (5% hold): 0.5x baseline error-rate + no sustained >20% p95 latency increase over 10 minutes.
- Gate B (25% hold): 0.3x baseline error-rate + p99 < 250ms increase sustained over 30 minutes.
- If gate fails: immediate rollback to previous config and call-out on #release-orchestra with brief diagnosis.

Quick operational runbook (day-of):
- 09:00 PT — Release steward confirms dry-run results and releases hold.
- 09:45 PT — Ops stage: clear merge queue and tag release group (mb-YYYYMMDD-xx).
- 10:00 PT — Slot A start (5% traffic). Observe metrics and run synthetic QA probes.
- 11:30 PT — Decision point: promote to Slot B or rollback.
- 12:00–13:00 PT — Lunch buffer + documentation updates.
- 13:00 PT — Slot B start (25% traffic). Expanded smoke tests run.
- 14:30 PT — Decision point: promote to full rollout OR expand internally to 60% for a BYO-customer test group.
- 15:30 PT — Final promote/rollback decision.
- 16:00 PT — Post-release notes drafted; open retrospective doc; capture learnings.

Risk and contingency lanes:
- Emergency lane (immediate rollback): feature flags reversible within 30s; automated rollbacks cover 80% of cases.
- Partial rollback: ability to disable individual items in the bundle without affecting others. Each ticket must include the kill-switch path.
- Escalation matrix: steward -> SRE on-call -> infra lead -> Eng manager -> Head of Release. Phone/Slack contact table included in ticket template.

Telemetry and SLOs to watch (priority):
- Ingress request rate by route, request error rate (4xx, 5xx), p50/p95/p99 latencies, model API token consumption, cost-per-1k-token estimate drift, KV cache hit%, batching efficiency, end-to-end tail latency for streaming sessions.
- Synthetic checks: 3 end-to-end scripts across regions (us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast) and a sample prompt set for quality regressions.

Release notes draft (brief snippet to include in customer-facing changelog):
- Title: Microbundle 2026-02-19 — Small stability and telemetry improvements
- Summary: This microbundle contains several non-breaking changes that improve batching stability, enrich telemetry tags for cost analysis, and tune the autoscaler for low-traffic tails. No API changes expected.
- Included items: RE-4821 (batcher stabilization), RE-4826 (telemetry tagging), RE-4829 (autoscaler low-traffic tuning).
- Impact: expected latency improvement in p95 for background jobs; temporary small increases in logging volume during rollout.

Post-release retro template (to capture after each microbundle):
- What went well: short bullet list.
- What surprised us: incidents, noisy alerts, unexpected rollbacks.
- Metrics snapshot: compare baseline vs post-release for p95, error-rate, cost-per-1k-token.
- Action items: owners, priority, ETA.

Operational notes and heuristics (house rules):
- Limit concurrent microbundles per week to 1 per critical product area (console, serving-runtime, console).
- No more than two microbundle items that touch the same backend service in a single window.
- If an item in the bundle is upgraded to high risk after planning cutover, it must be de-scoped.
- Use the tag "microbundle:YYYYMMDD" on every related PR and ticket.

Open questions and TODOs:
- Rollout tooling: can we automate the canary gate checks and decision via a small pipeline (proposal: RE-4902)?
- Cross-team blackout calendar enforcement: how strict should infra be about scheduling conflicts? (proposal: one-week penalty/requeue).
- Add a lightweight per-bundle QA checklist for Solutions Engineering for customer-visible features.

Appendix: quick templates (copy into ticket)
- Ticket release summary snippet (one-paragraph to go into changelog).
- Kill-switch steps (explicit CLI commands or flag toggles).
- Telemetry dashboard links (staging + prod) and synthetic probe IDs.

Notes to steward: this is intentionally compact. Iterate after two runs and we will move status to in_review. For next iteration, add an automated gating script and a simple dashboard that surfaces all pending microbundle conflicts across teams.

Document history:
- 2026-02-03: initial sketch (Aisha Kumar)
- 2026-02-10: added canary gate thresholds and sample calendar (Rafael Ortega)
- 2026-02-18: updated runbook times and added release notes template (Samira Patel)
